#!/bin/sh
# Makes build.nbt from scratch: build.mjs writes a temp file, which replaces build.nbt only if the build succeeds.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
tmp="build.tmp.$$.nbt"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
node build.mjs "$tmp"
mv "$tmp" build.nbt

input.summary: Store shell (parts/shell.mjs) is built and make.sh produces build.nbt with it; no edits were needed. Its own writes use only palette blocks: 738 placed, 0 refused, and it builds clean alone with no roof.
left: The OFF-PALETTE line still prints for this part: smooth_stone_stairs x40, andesite_slab x40, stone_slab x64. They come from the roof preset laid by runParts right after the shell (roof.json, the Roofs part), not from parts/shell.mjs. runParts files them under Store shell, so the line is misattributed. Fix belongs in roof.json or the roof preset, which is outside this part's scope and was not edited. Palette-listed swaps exist: smooth_stone_stairs to polished_andesite_stairs, andesite_slab to polished_andesite_slab, stone_slab to smooth_stone_slab.
REFUSED: none. Store shell wrote 0 refused cells, so no shell writes needed moving.

waste.what: Working out which part wrote the off-palette ids: I grepped shell.mjs for the three ids and then rebuilt the shell alone to show the roof was the source.
waste.cost: 2 extra node runs and a grep; no shell edits were made
waste.tool: runParts should tag roof-laid blocks in parts-report.json as their own entry (e.g. 'Roof (roof.json)') instead of the preceding part, and mcd roof should take a palette option so the modern preset emits palette-listed stairs and slabs.

waste.what: Looking up palette-listed replacements for the roof's stairs and slabs by hand.
waste.tool: mcd palette --suggest <off-palette id> (or a roof preset material map that already snaps to palette.json roles) would name the nearest palette block per id.

companions.task: Own roof.json: replace the preset's smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab and stone_slab with palette-listed blocks (polished_andesite_stairs, polished_andesite_slab, smooth_stone_slab), then re-run make.sh to clear the off-palette line.
